 import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = {

    'South Asia': [32.6, 33.5, 31.8, 30.9, 31.2, 31.5],
    'Southeast Asia': [43.2, 44.1, 42.3, 41.8, 42.5, 43.0],
    'Middle East': [47.5, 48.3, 46.7, 45.9, 46.2, 46.8],
    'Caribbean': [34.0, 35.2, 33.1, 32.5, 32.9, 33.4],
    'Northern Europe': [65.2, 66.1, 64.5, 65.3, 66.0, 66.8],
    'Western Europe': [58.7, 59.5, 57.8, 58.2, 59.1, 60.0],
    'East Asia': [52.3, 53.1, 51.6, 52.0, 52.7, 53.4],
    'Oceania': [44.1, 45.0, 43.2, 42.8, 43.5, 44.1]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df.set_index('Year', inplace=True)

fig = go.Figure()

regions = df.columns
colors = [
    '#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728', '#9467bd',
    '#8c564b', '#e377c2', '#7f7f7f', '#bcbd22', '#17becf',
    '#aec7e8', '#ffbb78', '#98df8a', '#ff9896', '#c5b0d5'
]

for region, color in zip(regions, colors):
    if region != 'South America':
        fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
            x=df.index,
            y=df[region],
            name=region,
            marker=dict(color=color)
        ))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Trends in Formal Employment Rates Across Regions (2018-2023)',
    xaxis_title='Year',
    yaxis_title='Unemployment Rate (%)',
    legend_title='Region',
    template='plotly_white',
    height=700,
    width=1000,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=60, t=80, b=60),

        yanchor='bottom',

        xanchor='right',
        x=1
    ),
    hovermode='x unified'
)

fig.write_image('output.png')
SUMMARY
 The image is a line chart titled *Trends in Formal Employment Rates Across Regions (2018-2023)*, illustrating how formal employment rates have evolved over a six-year period across fifteen global regions. The horizontal axis represents the years from 2018 to 2023, while the vertical axis measures the formal employment rate as a percentage, ranging from 25% to 70%.

Each region is represented by a distinct colored line and corresponding markers, making it easy to track changes over time. Northern Europe consistently exhibits the highest formal employment rates, starting at 65.2% in 2018 and gradually increasing to 66.8% by 2023. Eastern Europe follows closely, with rates beginning at 60.5% in 2018, dipping slightly in 2020, and then rising to 62.3% in 2023. Western Europe also maintains relatively high rates, starting at 58.7% and ending at 60.0% in 2023, with a minor decline in 2020.

East Asia’s formal employment rates show a steady upward trend, moving from 52.3% in 2018 to 53.4% in 2023. The Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Southern Africa display moderate rates, with the Middle East starting at 47.5% and ending at 46.8%, Southeast Asia fluctuating slightly around the low 40s, and Southern Africa decreasing from 45.8% to 43.2%. West Africa and Oceania follow similar downward trends, with West Africa dropping from 40.1% to 37.3% and Oceania from 44.1% to 44.1%, showing a slight recovery after 2020.

South Asia, the Caribbean, Central Africa, and East Africa all exhibit a gradual decline in formal employment rates over the six-year span. South Asia falls from 32.6% to 31.5%, the Caribbean from 34.0% to 33.4%, Central Africa from 38.2% to 34.7%, and East Africa from 36.7% to 33.2%. South America, which begins with the lowest rate at 30.5% in 2018, experiences a slight decline before stabilizing around 30.1% in 2023.

The chart uses a clean, white background with a horizontal legend positioned at the top for clarity, ensuring that the data remains the focal point. The lines are smooth and clearly distinguishable, with each region’s trend easily traceable through the use of consistent color coding and markers at each data point.

p = Path("chart.py")
s = p.read_text()
old = """    if region != 'South America':
        fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
            x=df.index,
            y=df[region],
            name=region,
            marker=dict(color=color)
        ))"""
new = """    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=df.index,
        y=df[region],
        name=region,
        mode='lines+markers',
        line=dict(color=color),
        marker=dict(color=color)
    ))"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)
s = s.replace("yaxis_title='Unemployment Rate (%)',", "yaxis_title='Formal Employment Rate (%)',\n    yaxis=dict(range=[25, 70]),")
p.write_text(s)
exec(compile(s, "chart.py", "exec"))
print("Trace count:", len(fig.data))
print("Title:", fig.layout.title.text)
print("Y axis:", fig.layout.yaxis.title.text, fig.layout.yaxis.range)
for trace, (region, values) in zip(fig.data, table.set_index('Year').items()):
    assert trace.name == region
    assert list(trace.x) == table.Year.tolist()
    assert list(trace.y) == values.tolist()
    assert trace.type == 'scatter' and trace.mode == 'lines+markers'
print("All traces match table.csv exactly.")
